title: Messerschmitt Bf 109 F-2 three-view (PDF Abb. 16) and Moelders F-2 profile (PDF Abb. 53)
frame: metres; X span (+X port), +Y up, +Z nose; z = 0 at mid length, y = 0 on the propeller axis

side.note: erase: antenna wire from the mast to the fin (it closes a false area above the spine) and the two drawn propeller blades; the model's blades are excluded likewise. u: spinner tip (px 7) to rudder trailing edge (px 461) = overall length 8.94 m (PDF table, Bf 109 F). v: same 50.78 px/m, zero on the spinner axis.

calibration.anisotropic: Span is calibrated to the PDF table (9.97 m) and length to the PDF table (8.94 m). The drawing itself is 533 px wide and 453 px long, a ratio 5.3 % above the table's. Measured on this drawing: wing area 16.46 m2 with these two scales (table 16.1 m2) but 15.62 m2 at the span scale alone; propeller diameter 2.94 m at the length scale (3.0 m VDM) but 2.79 m at the span scale. So the fuselage, heights and propeller follow the length scale and only the span is stretched to the table.

top.note: Plan view rotated a quarter turn, nose up, starboard right (pitot on the port wing at the left). erase: the two drawn blades beside the spinner.

calibration.anisotropic: Span to the PDF table (9.97 m, 535 px); heights at the side view's length scale (50.78 px/m) for the reason given in the plan view: the drawing's own scale is uniform, the table disagrees with its span/length ratio by 5.3 %.

front.note: outsideSeeds: the empty triangles that the two upper drawn blades close off against the tailplane and fuselage.
front.ignoreNote: Blades are not compared in any view. In this front view the drawn blades stand at 179.9, -57.6 and +58.0 deg from the hub (measured on the mask), i.e. 112/124/124 deg apart, which no rigid three-blade rotor can match. Each polygon follows one drawn blade from just outside the spinner ring (17 px) to its tip + 2 px, half width = widest projected blade chord / 2 + 2 px; inside it model and drawing are set equal. The spinner is compared.
